title: HomeGuard Homeowners Policy: Roof Surfacing Reversal Payment Calculation
content:
**Claims Manual, HomeGuard Homeowners Policy: the amount of a roof surfacing reversal payment.** This page fixes the figure paid when the wind or hail roof surfacing damage on a HomeGuard claim, recorded only as a below-deductible denial, is re-settled.

## 1. Clause

1.1 **The claim.** The claim concerned is the one whose first-notice entry is the latest on the policy. Its date of loss, report date and cause of loss are those recorded on that first-notice entry.

1.2 **The damage figures.** The replacement-cost value and the depreciation of the roof surfacing are the figures recorded on the below-deductible denial entry of the roof surfacing on that claim.

1.3 **The occurrence deductible.** For a wind or hail loss, the occurrence deductible is the larger of (a) the wind/hail percentage on the declarations applied to Coverage A and (b) the tier's wind/hail deductible minimum. For every other cause of loss it is the all-other-perils deductible on the declarations.

1.4 **Deductible waiver.** No deductible applies when the replacement-cost values recorded on the claim's denial entries and on its payment entries that replace no denial, taken together, reach the tier's deductible waiver threshold, on a tier whose threshold is above 0.

1.5 **Deductible absorbed.** Otherwise the roof surfacing absorbs the smaller of the occurrence deductible and its covered amount.

1.6 **Covered amount.** The covered amount follows the roof surfacing settlement basis the declarations carry for the term:
- on the **roof surfacing schedule**, it is the replacement-cost value multiplied by the schedule percentage for the roof's age band;
- on **replacement cost**, it is the full replacement-cost value when that value is at or below the tier's no-holdback threshold, and otherwise the replacement-cost value less the recorded depreciation.

1.7 **Roof age for the band.** The roof's age is the calendar year of the date of loss minus the roof install year on the declarations.

1.8 **Schedule percentage.**

| Roof age at the date of loss (years) | Schedule percentage |
|---|---|
| 0 to 10 | 100 |
| 11 to 12 | 85 |
| 13 to 14 | 75 |
| 15 to 16 | 65 |
| 17 to 18 | 55 |
| 19 to 20 | 45 |
| 21 to 24 | 35 |
| 25 or more | 25 |

1.9 **The payment.** The reversal payment on the roof surfacing is the covered amount, less the deductible the roof surfacing absorbs, less any roof surfacing money already issued on the claim. It is never below 0.00, and it is rounded to the cent once, on the final figure.

## 2. Reading the band table at its edges

The bands are closed at both ends and adjoin without a gap. A roof aged exactly 10 years takes 100 percent and one aged 11 takes 85; a roof aged 20 takes 45 and one aged 21 takes 35; a roof aged 24 takes 35 and one aged 25 or more takes 25. Because the age is a difference of calendar years, the month and day of the loss do not move a roof between bands: a roof installed in 2009 is 15 years old for any loss dated in 2024.

## 3. Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

The inputs below are chosen for illustration only; they are not company figures.

**Example A, roof surfacing schedule, wind or hail loss.** Recorded replacement-cost value 12000.00, recorded depreciation 4800.00; roof installed 2005, date of loss in 2024, so the roof age is 19 and the schedule percentage 45. Covered amount: 12000.00 multiplied by 45 percent, which is 5400.00. Coverage A of 300000 at a wind/hail percentage of 1 gives 3000.00; with a wind/hail deductible minimum assumed at 1000.00 for the example, the occurrence deductible is the larger, 3000.00. The waiver threshold is taken as 0 for the example, so no waiver. Deductible absorbed: the smaller of 3000.00 and 5400.00, which is 3000.00. No roof surfacing money has been issued on the claim. Payment: 5400.00 less 3000.00 less 0.00, which is 2400.00.

**Example B, replacement cost, above the no-holdback threshold.** Recorded replacement-cost value 8000.00, depreciation 2000.00, no-holdback threshold assumed at 2500 for the example. The value is above the threshold, so the covered amount is 8000.00 less 2000.00, which is 6000.00. An all-other-perils deductible of 1000.00 is assumed for the example: absorbed 1000.00. Payment 5000.00.

**Example C, the floor.** Covered amount 1200.00 and an occurrence deductible of 2500.00: the roof surfacing absorbs 1200.00 and, with nothing already issued, the payment is 0.00. Where roof surfacing money of 300.00 had already been issued on the claim, the figure before the floor would be less than 0.00, and the payment is still 0.00.

## 4. Points of judgement

- *Which first-notice entry governs when the policy has several claims?* The latest first-notice entry on the policy identifies the claim; its recorded date of loss, report date and cause of loss are used as they stand.
- *Does the waiver test count only the roof?* No. It adds the replacement-cost values on every denial entry of the claim and on every payment entry of the claim that replaces no denial.
- *When is the rounding done?* Once, on the final figure; intermediate figures such as the covered amount are carried unrounded.
